final_assessment:
External iteration 1 (GPT-5 Codex) walked to zero: 3 CRITICAL, 2 WARNING, 1 SUGGESTION, none stale. Three went through the decision lane with chat ratification (C1 option C, C3 option B, W1 option C); three were obvious-fix.

THE PATTERN, AND IT IS ABOUT THE PREVIOUS WALK RATHER THAN THE PROPOSAL. Three of the six findings are wake from the fresh pass's own fixes. C2 exists BECAUSE F5's reorder moved the engine removals after the bodies and stranded the only build in the middle — a reorder that closed one ordering hazard opened another, and nothing re-checked the build step when work crossed it. C1 is the descope-sweep corollary failing on my own edit: I replaced the coexistence paragraph with the totality rule and never looked UP at the definition governing it, and my own sweep (4.5) greps `coexist`/`strict widening`/`GATE_FIELD_PAIRS`, none of which appear in a definitional clause. W1 is F9 applied faithfully to a derivation that did not guarantee what F9 claimed — preserving a raw `JSON.parse` as the 'standing regression pin' for prior-generation readability, when it only ever proved JSON parses as JSON. The fresh pass named this shape as 'a boundary drawn one line short'; the external pass found three more instances of it, inside the fixes.

C1 IS THE SHARPEST AND THE FIX IS SMALLER THAN THE FINDING PROPOSED. The requirement excluded a zero-citation record because it 'has no ordering to check'. Edge (d) makes that reason false — an empty citation IS checked, against the trail. So the exclusion was re-grounded on CADENCE POSITION, which is what it always meant, rather than broadening the qualifying test (weakening 'cite your evidence') or moving the carrier (D-rc04c-1's already-rejected two-records-for-one-fact).

C3 IS UNRESOLVED IN SUBSTANCE AND DELIBERATELY SO. The ruling is drafted at task 5.1c and NOT performed, because rulings are architect-owned; it GATES this stage, since until it lands R-crc-1 says an over-ceiling proposal is split before review rather than reviewed. The draft is split honestly: the byte ceiling is proposed to measure CHANGED bytes (the format forces verbatim carriage of full requirement bodies, and ~43 KB of this delta is exactly that), while the TASK overage is proposed as R-crc-9's first ratified breach rather than defined away. The figures ROSE during this walk — 56,262 B / 30 tasks when the finding was written, 57,418 B / 34 now — and that is recorded in both the task and the proposal rather than restated at the smaller number, because a ceiling argument that quietly cites stale figures is the failure this stage keeps finding in others.

ONE TRAIL CONDITION worth naming for whoever reads this next: the change carries TWO `external-proposal-*.md` files for iteration 1 (02-10-20Z and 02-21-43Z), the same reviewer's first run and its sharpened re-run. This walk ingested 02-21-43Z, the strict superset. The gate keys on 02-10-20Z, whose five findings are all genuinely resolved by the same edits but under different titles, so a separate coverage record follows this one rather than leaving a resolved pass reading unresolved. That the trail counts both as independent spend (now 3) is a real effect of a reviewer re-running rather than editing in place, and it is worth knowing before reading the spend figure as three distinct reviews.
